subject: Post-demo recap & technical follow-up: embeddings, reranker, streaming semantics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@streamly.ai>, Ethan Cole <ethan@streamly.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap & technical follow-up: embeddings, reranker, streaming semantics

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can make the technical workshop productive.

High-level summary from our end:
- Goal: Bring semantic search + concise synthesis into Streamly product flows (user query -> embed + recall -> rerank -> synth tool-call to source system).
- Constraints you flagged: 60 qps sustained, bursts up to ~200 qps; p95 latency SLO ~300ms; documents ~800–1,400 tokens typical; strict PII controls (no unredacted logs to third-party).

Open technical questions / clarifications we need from you before hands-on workshop:
1) Candidate set size: do you expect to recall 100–1,000 documents per query? (affects embedding retrieval latency and memory footprint)
2) Reranker budget: is a 50-top cross-encoder acceptable (i.e., cheap recall at dot-product, expensive cross-encoder for 50)?
3) Structured output: do you need JSON/tool-calling for the final synthesis (e.g., {source_refs:[], summary, action_items}) or plain text?
4) Streaming: do you require partial token streaming to the client for UX, or can you accept server-side aggregation and then one-shot responses?
5) Auth & deployment: will this be piloted on Redwood hosted or Private (VPC/on-prem)? Private affects auth options (mTLS/KMS) and routing.

Proposed next steps:
- You: share a small, anonymized sample (3–5 queries + ground-truth passages). Thanks for offering that — please attach when you can.
- Redwood: produce a lightweight architecture proposal (we'll include two alternatives: low-latency recall-first vs strong cross-encoder rerank) + rough cost/latency estimates.
- Book a 90-min technical workshop with engineering + infra (proposed: Wed 12/8 10am PT).

I also tossed two small attachments with call notes and our quickstart for embeddings. If any of the decisions above are off, flag them and we'll adjust before the workshop.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-embed.pdf (overview), postcall-ma.pdf (notes)

From: Samira Khan <samira@streamly.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan@streamly.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & technical follow-up: embeddings, reranker, streaming semantics

Thanks, Ben — great summary. Couple quick clarifications inline and a dataset attached.

Inline answers:
- Candidate set: we typically recall ~200 documents for a full product flow, occasionally 800 for deep research queries. Memory/latency trade-off is key.
- Reranker: 50-top cross-encoder sounds reasonable as a starting point. We care more about precision in top-5.
- Structured output: yes, we need JSON with explicit source references (source_id + offset) and a small list of action items; our UI expects a structured payload to render highlights. Example: {"summary":"...","sources":[{"id":"doc-123","snippet":"..."}],"actions":["jump-to-doc"]}.
- Streaming: user-facing product shows incremental results so streaming tokens are helpful, but we can compromise on streaming just for the initial MVP and add continuous streaming later.
- Deployment: pilot on Redwood hosted, but data cannot leave region and any PII must be filtered at ingestion. If pilot goes well, we'll discuss Private.

Attached: streamly_sample_100.zip (anonymized subset, 100 docs + 10 queries).

Open Qs for Redwood team:
1) For tokenization budgets, can you share an estimator (we want to understand how our 1.2k token docs translate to model input limits when combined with prompt + tool-calls)?
2) For streaming semantics: if we stream tokens, how do you handle partial structured output (e.g., partial JSON events) — do you recommend chunked JSON or final assembled JSON?

Samira
Head of Search Product | Streamly
samira@streamly.ai

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 3:10 PM Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can make the technical workshop productive.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@streamly.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan@streamly.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 19:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & technical follow-up: embeddings, reranker, streaming semantics

Thanks for the dataset, Samira — gave it a quick scan. A few practical recommendations and example schemas that should help answer the tokenization/streaming questions.

1) Chat vs completions:
- Use chat endpoint when you have multi-turn state and tool-calling/structured responses (we support function/tool calls that return typed payloads). Chat frames are also friendlier for system/user roles.
- Use completions for single-shot generation (prompt -> response) where you manage the prompt construction. Completions may be marginally simpler for very high-QPS stateless requests.

2) Tokenization & max_tokens heuristics:
- Example: model context limit = 4096 tokens. If your doc avg = 1,200 tokens and you recall 200 docs, you MUST pre-select with embeddings (dense recall) and truncate to top-K content for the LM prompt.
- Practical pipeline: recall 200 (embedding dot-prod) -> assemble top 20 passages (context ~ 2,800 tokens) -> prepend system & user (500 tokens) -> reserve max_tokens= 600 for generation. That keeps you under ~4096.

3) stop sequences and streaming semantics:
- stop sequences: use short explicit tokens (e.g., "\\n\\n---END---") if you need deterministic termination. For JSON outputs, a separate close token helps parsing.
- streaming: Redwood streams tokens as delta events (token, token_index, is_final=false) then a final is_final=true event. For structured outputs we recommend emitting interim objects as top-level events ("partial_json": "{...}"), but that requires the client to do incremental JSON assembly. Alternative: stream raw tokens and assemble server-side into a final JSON; this is simpler but delays structured rendering.

4) embeddings + reranker topology (latency vs quality):
- Suggested two-stage: cheap vector recall (text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims) -> dot product top-500 -> light lexical filter -> cross-encoder rerank top-50 (cross-encoder is heavier but much better for top-5 precision).
- If you need sub-300ms p95, we can push reranker down to top-50 with a fast cross-encoder on GPU-backed Dedicated pool. Consider caching the reranker outputs for identical queries.

5) auth & routing notes:
- Hosted: API keys with per-key quotas; for elevated security you can enable IP allowlists and per-route model pinning.
- Private: mTLS + KMS/HSM integration; we can also enable audit logs.
- Routing: we can route by latency or cost; i.e., low-latency path -> smaller model variant, else fallback to cheaper model.

Example request/response schema (chat + tool-call style) — note: inline JSON below is illustrative:

REQUEST (chat call):
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"You are a concise summarizer that returns JSON."},
    {"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following sources and list source refs."},
    {"role":"tool","name":"recall_docs","content":"[doc-231, doc-77, doc-12]"}
  ],
  "stream": true,
  "max_tokens": 600,
  "stop": ["\\n\\n---END---"]
}

RESPONSE (streamed tokens events):
{
  "event": "token", "token": "{", "idx": 1, "is_final": false
} ...
{
  "event": "token", "token": "}", "idx": 132, "is_final": true
}

If you need strict JSON messages for the UI, we can instead recommend the model emit a single final JSON snippet and set stream=false; this simplifies parsing at the cost of latency.

6) operational things for the workshop:
- Please confirm expected QPS distribution (we saw 60 sustained, 200 burst) and whether burst capacity needs to be served from the same SLA pool.
- If PII is present, please share your preferred redaction approach (client-side remove vs server-side tokenization hooks).

I attached a quick CSV with rough latency estimates for reranker top-K sizes (reranker-latency-estimates.csv). Happy to pair during the workshop to run a small live eval on your sample.

—
Karthik Iyer
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & technical follow-up: embeddings, reranker, streaming semantics

Samira / Ethan — great, thanks for the dataset and quick answers.

Quick confirmation of decisions and owners:
- Recall topology: dense recall -> top-200 -> candidate pruning -> rerank top-50 (Owner: Karthik).
- Structured output: JSON required for UI; we will prototype server-side assembly first, later add token streaming for incremental display (Owner: Ben + Streamly eng).
- Streaming: MVP = server-side assemble (stream=false). If the performance numbers hold we'll enable token streaming for progressive UX.
- Auth & pilot: Redwood hosted for pilot; data stays in US region; Samira to confirm PII redaction approach.

Action items:
- Samira: confirm PII approach + schedule for the 90-min workshop (Samira to propose time window by EOD Thu).
- Karthik: prepare a short demo script (recall->rerank->synthesis) and the latency/cost delta for top-20 vs top-50 rerank.
- Ben: produce the architecture slide with two alternatives + a sample request/response schema.

I'll schedule the workshop once Samira confirms times. Thanks everyone — looking forward to building this together.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com
